claim: Predicted edges with dt != 1 (gaps, backward, same-frame, self) are silently DROPPED by the scorer before counting - neither TP nor FP nor FN - contradicting the official metrics.md and the organisers' own test docstring, which say they count as false positives.

claim: The only way to recover a missed detection is to INTERPOLATE THE NODE and emit two dt=1 edges: a gap edge scores identically to predicting nothing (0.000 vs 0.000), while an interpolated node inside the radius restores J=1.000.
quote: Drawing the gap edge scores exactly the same as drawing nothing (0.000 both). Inserting an interpolated node inside the radius restores the full 1.000. Miss the radius and you pay 2 FPs instead. With median step 1.8 um against a 7 um radius, linear interpolation between t-1 and t+1 lands inside

claim: A single duplicate detection 0.4 um from a real cell HALVES the edge Jaccard (1.000 -> 0.500): only one twin can win the one-to-one match and the loser's edges are still graded, so they become FPs. NMS quality outranks every other lever.
quote: a duplicate detection halves the score. Only one of the two twins can win the one-to-one match; the loser's edges still touch annotated evidence, so they are graded as FPs. 1.000 -> 0.500 from one extra peak 0.4 um away.

claim: Centroid precision has a measured cliff at sigma ~2 um, far below the 7 um match radius: 1.5 um is free, 2.5 um costs 16%, 3 um costs 41%, 4 um costs 74% - driven by ~9-10 um inter-cell spacing, not cell size, and identical in both embryos.
quote: The cliff is at sigma ~= 2 um — about 1.2 voxels in z and 5 voxels in xy. Below 1.5 um it is free; at 2.5 um you have lost 16 %; at 3 um, 41 %; at 4 um, 74 %. The curve is essentially identical for both embryos ... The failure is driven by inter-cell spacing, not cell size.

claim: A metric term that rewards absence cannot be validated on sparse labels: deleting a track only registers a cost if that track happened to be annotated, so the labels confirm the reward but never the price.

A metric term that rewards absence is the hardest kind to validate on sparse labels. The labels can confirm the reward. They cannot confirm the price.

If you're testing anything that reduces output volume, check what fraction of what you removed was even labelled, before you believe the score.

claim: Adoptable diagnostic: split_score(J, n_pred, n_est) decomposes adjusted edge Jaccard into the raw Jaccard and the node-count multiplier, flagging any change where >70% of the delta came from the multiplier as unproven.

The split_score replica formula matches the official scorer exactly - support/metrics.py computes adj_edge_jaccard = max(0.0, edge_jaccard * (1 - ADJUSTMENT_ALPHA * total_node_ratio)) with ALPHA=0.1 and no upper clip - so the offline/LB divergence is a label-sparsity effect, not a scorer mismatch.

claim: The 7 um match radius is anisotropic in voxels: 4.3 voxels in z but 17.2 voxels in x/y, because z is 4x coarser (1.625 vs 0.40625 um/voxel), so the same voxel error costs 4x more in z.

quote: Frame-to-frame displacement: median 1.82 µm, 95th percentile 5.34 µm, 99th percentile 8.38 µm. A nearest-neighbour linker with a radius of 8.4 µm can reach 99% of the true links. In voxels that is about 21 in x/y and 5 in z

claim: UNTAKEN IDEA: the public 0.908 pipelines inherit the metric's 7.0 um node-matching gate as their LINKING gate, but the two are unrelated - the scorer never checks predicted edge length - so a 7 um motion gate discards ~2% of true links for free.
quote: The public 0.908 pipelines use 7.0 µm as their linking gate as well. It reads like a recommendation. It is not — it is the tolerance for *node position error*, and using it as a *motion* gate throws away every true link longer than 7 µm.

claim: UNTAKEN IDEA: the 7 um motion-gate loss is per-movie, not per-link, so a per-movie gate set from that movie's own p99 candidate distance beats any global constant.
quote: A fifth of the movies lose nothing at 7 µm; a third lose more than 2%, and the worst loses one link in seven. A global gate tuned on the pooled distribution is tuned for the median movie and wrong for exactly the movies where it matters.

claim: Of the true links a 7 um gate discards, about two-thirds are fast in-plane motion and one-third are z-dominated with a median of three z-voxels, so a neighbourhood expressed in 'voxels in every direction' fails on the tall minority.
quote: Of the links a 7 µm gate discards, about two-thirds are cells moving fast across the plane and one-third are dominated by z — a median of three z-voxels, which is exactly the kind of step a search neighbourhood expressed in "voxels in every direction" would fail to reach.
